concepts.title: Why Elections Matter in a Democracy

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Why Elections Matter in a Democracy' refers to.
questions.a: Elections are essential to a democratic system because they convert the people's will into a government: citizens choose their representatives, reward or punish performance, and keep power changing hands peacefully.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Why Elections Matter in a Democracy'.
questions.a: Elections are democracy's heartbeat: votes decide who rules and how long.

concepts.title: The Election Machinery: Commission and Process

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'The Election Machinery: Commission and Process' refers to.
questions.a: An independent Election Commission supervises elections: preparing voter rolls, announcing schedules, enforcing the model code of conduct, overseeing campaigning, polling and counting - so that the whole process stays free, fair and uniform across the country.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'The Election Machinery: Commission and Process'.
questions.a: A referee above the players: the Election Commission keeps the contest fair.

questions.q: Under which section is 'The Election Machinery: Commission and Process' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 7 (source: iest107.txt sections on the election commission and process)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Challenges and the Citizen's Role' refers to.
questions.a: Elections face challenges of money power, muscle power, fake promises and uneven turnout; a vigilant citizen answers by voting without inducement, questioning candidates, checking information and participating beyond election day.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Challenges and the Citizen's Role'.
questions.a: A vote is a trust: informed, un bribed voting is the citizen's duty to democracy.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Challenges and the Citizen's Role' taught, and from which source text?
